statement: Square ABCD has side 12 cm, with its corners in the order A, B, C, D around the square. Point E lies on side BC with BE = 8 cm, and point F lies on side CD with DF = 3 cm. What is the area of triangle AEF, in square centimetres?

choices.misconception: I found the total area of the three corner triangles and gave that instead of what is left.
I assumed that a triangle drawn from a corner of the square always takes up half of it.
I forgot to halve the 4 by 9 rectangle for the triangle at corner C, so I took away 36 there instead of 18.
I mixed up BE and EC and used BE = 4 cm, which changes two of the corner triangles.

hints: Triangle AEF is the square with three right-angled triangles cut off.
Draw the square and mark E and F. The three corner triangles at B, C and D are right-angled, so their areas are easy. Subtract them from the area of the square.
The corner triangles have legs 12 and 8, then 12 and 3, then EC = 4 and FC = 9.

solutions.reliable: The square has area 144. Around triangle AEF are three right-angled triangles: ABE with legs 12 and 8, area 48; ADF with legs 12 and 3, area 18; and ECF with legs EC = 12 - 8 = 4 and FC = 12 - 3 = 9, area 18. So triangle AEF has area 144 - 48 - 18 - 18 = 60 square centimetres. The transferable idea: a slanted triangle inside a rectangle is often easiest as the rectangle minus right-angled corner pieces.

whyOnTest: Tests area by subtraction: a tilted triangle is hard to measure directly but easy as a square minus three right-angled corners.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
